es.B: Noemí, su suegra, le dijo: «Hija mía, ¿no es hora de que te busque un hogar estable, donde te vaya bien?
es.R: Un día Noemí le dijo a Rut: «Hija mía, quiero encontrarte un esposo y un hogar donde estés segura y bien cuidada.

fr.B: Noémi, sa belle-mère, lui dit : « Ma fille, n’est-il pas temps que je te cherche un foyer où tu sois heureuse ?
fr.R: Un jour, Noémi a dit à Ruth : « Ma fille, je veux te trouver un mari et une maison, où tu seras en sécurité et où l’on prendra soin de toi.

ko.L: 시어머니 나오미가 룻에게 말했다. "내 딸아, 너를 위하여 안식할 곳을 찾아 주어서 네가 잘되게 해야 하지 않겠느냐?
ko.B: 시어머니 나오미가 룻에게 말했다. "내 딸아, 이제는 내가 너를 위해 편히 지낼 보금자리를 찾아 주어서, 네가 잘살게 해 주어야 하지 않겠느냐?
ko.R: 어느 날 나오미가 룻에게 말했다. "내 딸아, 나는 너에게 남편과 가정을 찾아 주고 싶다. 그러면 네가 안전하게 보살핌을 받으며 살 수 있을 것이다.

pt.L: E Noemi, a sua sogra, lhe disse: "Minha filha, não devo eu buscar para você um lugar de descanso, para que tudo lhe vá bem?
pt.B: Noemi, a sua sogra, lhe disse: "Minha filha, não está na hora de eu procurar para você um lar onde você tenha descanso e onde a sua vida vá bem?
pt.R: Um dia Noemi disse a Rute: "Minha filha, eu quero encontrar um marido e um lar para você, onde você esteja segura e seja bem cuidada.

decisions.choice: a resting place: a settled home in marriage
decisions.reason: The word means a place of rest, a secure home. Naomi has already prayed that each of her daughters-in-law would find rest "in the house of her husband" (1:9), with a word from the same root. Now she sets out to bring that about for Ruth.

decisions.choice: should I not seek: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying "I must". Naomi speaks as the older woman responsible for her widowed daughter-in-law; in that world a marriage was arranged by the family, not by the bride alone.

decisions.choice: a husband and a home ... safe and cared for
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the resting place is (decision m1) and turns the question that expects yes into a statement of what Naomi wants. "Ruth" is named for "her".

decisions.choice: um lugar de descanso (L); um lar onde você tenha descanso (B)
decisions.reason: "Descanso" takes up the word of Naomi's wish in 1:9 (m1), so the reader sees that she now sets out to bring it about; Balanced adds "lar", the settled home that rest means here. Readable says what it is, as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: And now, [is] not Boaz our relative, with whose young women you were? Look, he [is] winnowing the threshing floor of the barley tonight.

en.L: And now, is not Boaz our relative, whose young women you were with? Look, he is winnowing [at] the threshing floor of the barley tonight.
en.B: Now Boaz, whose young women you have been working with, is our relative, is he not? Tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
en.R: You know that Boaz is one of our relatives, and you have been working with his young women. Tonight he will be at the threshing floor, winnowing barley. He will toss the grain into the air so the wind can blow the husks away.

es.B: Ahora bien, Booz, con cuyas criadas has estado trabajando, es pariente nuestro, ¿no es así? Esta noche va a aventar la cebada en la era.

fr.B: Booz, avec les servantes de qui tu as travaillé, est notre parent, n’est-ce pas ? Ce soir, il vanne l’orge sur l’aire.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, Bô-ô, người mà con đã ở với các thiếu nữ của ông ấy, chẳng phải là bà con của chúng ta sao? Kìa, đêm nay ông ấy sảy lúa mạch tại sân đập lúa.

decisions.choice: our relative: a member of the family circle
decisions.reason: The word names a relative or close acquaintance. Naomi has already told Ruth that Boaz is one of their redeemers (2:20; see also 2:1). Saying "our" relative, she includes Ruth in the family.

decisions.choice: winnowing at night: separating grain from chaff in the evening breeze
decisions.reason: After threshing, the grain and chaff were thrown into the air with a fork so the wind carried off the light chaff while the heavy grain fell back. The evening breeze was used for the work. The threshing floor was a hard, open place outside the town (verse 15 says Boaz then went into the town), and the owner and workers often slept there to guard the grain.

decisions.choice: He will toss the grain into the air so the wind can blow the husks away.
decisions.reason: Readable explains what winnowing is, since many readers will not know the word. It turns Naomi's question that expects yes into a statement.

decisions.choice: "uwanja wa kupuria" for the threshing floor; "kupepeta" for winnowing
decisions.reason: As agreed for these books in every language: "uwanja wa kupuria" is the open, hard floor where grain is beaten out, and "kupepeta" the everyday Swahili word for tossing grain so that the chaff blows away.

decisions.choice: "la era"; "aventar"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: the threshing floor is "la era", the flat open place where grain was threshed and winnowed, and "aventar" is the Spanish word for tossing the grain into the wind (m2).

decisions.choice: "l'aire"; "vanner"
alternatives: "le lieu où l'on bat le grain" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the terms note for these books sets, the threshing floor is "l'aire" at every level; it is the place of chapters 3 and 4. Readable explains winnowing, as the English Readable does, so the word "aire" can stay.

decisions.choice: "sân đập lúa" for the threshing floor; "sảy lúa" for winnowing
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note; "sảy" is the Vietnamese word for separating grain from chaff, which Readable also describes.

decisions.choice: "타작마당" (threshing floor)
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set.

decisions.choice: joeirar (L); abanar (B, R); a eira (every level)
decisions.reason: "Joeirar" is the exact Portuguese word for winnowing (m2) but is little known, so Literal alone keeps it; Balanced says "abanar", the everyday farm word, and Readable explains it, as the English Readable does. "A eira" is the ordinary word for the threshing floor, kept through the chapter.

pt.L: Lave-se, pois, e unja-se, e ponha as suas roupas sobre você, e desça à eira; não se dê a conhecer ao homem até que ele acabe de comer e de beber.
pt.B: Tome banho, passe óleo perfumado, vista-se bem e desça à eira. Mas não deixe que o homem a veja até ele terminar de comer e beber.
pt.R: Tome banho, passe perfume e vista a sua melhor roupa. Depois desça até a eira, mas fique num lugar onde ele não possa ver você até ele terminar de comer e beber.

decisions.choice: your garments ... you will go down: the readings of the margin (qere)
alternatives: and I will go down (the written text, read as Naomi's words about herself)
decisions.reason: Two words in this verse are written one way and read another. The written text (ketiv) has "your garment", one garment, perhaps an outer cloak; the margin (qere) reads "your garments". The written text also has a form that looks like "and I will go down"; the margin reads "and you will go down". The written form is most likely an older spelling of the "you" form for a woman, which the margin brings up to date, since Ruth goes down alone (verse 6) and Naomi stays at home (verse 16). The margin is followed in both places.

decisions.choice: wash, anoint, put on garments: making ready, perhaps putting off mourning
decisions.reason: Washing, rubbing the skin with scented oil and putting on clothes are the steps David takes when his time of mourning ends (2 Samuel 12:20), and those a bride's adornment is described with (Ezekiel 16:9-10). Ruth, a widow, is to make herself ready to present herself as a woman free to marry.

decisions.choice: do not make yourself known: keep out of sight until he has eaten
decisions.reason: Ruth is to wait until Boaz has had his meal and lies down (verse 4). She is not to be seen by the man while the workers are about, and the request comes when he is alone and at ease (verse 7).

decisions.choice: dress yourself well / dress in your best clothes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "put your garments on you", kept at Literal. Coming after the washing and the oil, it means dressing with care (decision m2), which Balanced and Readable say.

vi.R: Hãy để ý xem ông ấy nằm ngủ ở đâu. Rồi đến đó, lật tấm áo choàng nơi chân ông lên, và nằm xuống đó. Ông ấy sẽ cho con biết phải làm gì tiếp."

ko.L: 그가 누우면 그가 눕는 곳을 잘 보아 두었다가, 들어가서 그의 발치를 들추고 누워라. 그러면 네가 해야 할 일을 그가 너에게 말해 줄 것이다."
ko.B: 그가 누우면 그 자리를 잘 보아 두어라. 그런 다음 그에게 가서 그의 발치 이불을 들추고 거기에 누워라. 그러면 네가 어떻게 해야 할지 그가 말해 줄 것이다."
ko.R: 그가 어디에 누워 자는지 잘 보아 두어라. 그런 다음 그에게 가서 그의 겉옷을 젖혀 발을 드러내고 거기에 누워라. 그러면 다음에 무엇을 해야 할지 그가 알려 줄 것이다."

pt.L: E, quando ele se deitar, repare no lugar onde ele se deitar; então entre, e descubra os pés dele, e deite-se; e ele lhe dirá o que você deve fazer."
pt.B: Quando ele se deitar, observe bem o lugar onde ele está deitado. Depois vá até ele, descubra os pés dele e deite-se ali. Ele lhe dirá o que você deve fazer."
pt.R: Observe onde ele vai se deitar para dormir. Depois vá até ele, descubra os pés dele, dobrando para trás a capa dele, e deite-se ali. Ele vai dizer a você o que fazer depois."

decisions.choice: uncover his feet: turn back the covering from the place of his feet
alternatives: uncover the place of his legs
a veiled way of saying she is to offer herself to him
decisions.reason: The word for "feet" here is not the common one; it means the place of the feet, the area at a sleeper's feet and legs (the same word comes in Daniel 10:6 for the legs). Ruth is to fold back Boaz's cloak there and lie down at his feet, the place of a servant. It is a silent request that he will understand when he wakes. "Feet" can be a modest way of naming the private parts elsewhere (Isaiah 7:20), and the words "lie down", "know" and "uncover" can all carry a sexual sense, so the scene is told with tension. But the story shows nothing improper happening: Boaz praises Ruth as a woman of worth (verse 11), keeps her safe till morning, and protects her name (verse 14).

decisions.choice: and lie down: the reading of the margin (qere)
alternatives: and I will lie down (the written text)
decisions.reason: As with "go down" in verse 3, the written text has a form that looks like "and I will lie down"; the margin reads "and you will lie down". The written form is most likely the older spelling of the "you" form for a woman, and the margin is followed.

decisions.choice: he will tell you what you are to do: Boaz is to answer
decisions.reason: Naomi leaves the next step to Boaz. In the event Ruth speaks first and tells him what she asks (verse 9), and he answers (verses 10-13).

decisions.choice: by turning back his cloak
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of uncovering his feet and says what the act was (decision m1), so that the reader does not imagine something else.

en.B: Ruth answered her, "I will do everything you tell me."
en.R: Ruth said, "I will do everything you say."

es.L: Y ella le dijo: «Todo lo que me dices haré».
es.B: Rut le respondió: «Haré todo lo que me digas».
es.R: Rut le dijo: «Haré todo lo que me dices».

fr.L: Et elle lui dit : « Tout ce que tu me dis, je le ferai. »
fr.B: Ruth lui répondit : « Je ferai tout ce que tu me dis. »
fr.R: Ruth a dit : « Je ferai tout ce que tu dis. »

vi.L: Nàng nói với bà: "Mọi điều mẹ bảo con, con sẽ làm."
vi.B: Ru-tơ đáp: "Con sẽ làm mọi điều mẹ bảo."
vi.R: Ru-tơ nói: "Con sẽ làm mọi điều mẹ nói."

ko.L: 룻이 시어머니에게 말했다. "어머님이 저에게 말씀하신 대로 다 하겠어요."
ko.B: 룻이 대답했다. "어머님이 말씀하신 대로 다 하겠어요."

pt.L: E ela lhe disse: "Tudo o que você me disser, eu farei."
pt.B: Rute lhe respondeu: "Farei tudo o que você me disser."
pt.R: Rute disse: "Vou fazer tudo o que você disser."

decisions.choice: to me: read in the margin (qere) though not written
decisions.reason: The words "to me" are not written in the text; the margin tells the reader to say them. They make no difference to the meaning. The same happens in verse 17.

decisions.choice: all that you say I will do
decisions.reason: Ruth's answer is matched by Boaz's words to her in verse 11, "all that you say I will do for you". She trusts Naomi; Boaz will keep faith with Ruth.

decisions.choice: Ruth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, since "she" and "her" are both women.

source.text: וַתֵּ֖רֶד הַגֹּ֑רֶן וַתַּ֕עַשׂ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוַּ֖תָּה חֲמוֹתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went down [to] the threshing floor and did according to all that had commanded her her mother-in-law.

en.L: So she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.
en.B: So she went down to the threshing floor and did exactly as her mother-in-law had instructed her.
en.R: So Ruth went down to the threshing floor and did just what her mother-in-law had told her.

sw.L: Basi akashuka uwanjani pa kupuria, akafanya sawasawa na yote aliyomwagiza mama mkwe wake.
sw.B: Basi alishuka uwanjani pa kupuria, akafanya sawasawa na alivyoagizwa na mama mkwe wake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Ruthu alishuka uwanjani pa kupuria, akafanya kama mama mkwe wake alivyomwambia.

es.L: Y bajó a la era e hizo conforme a todo lo que su suegra le había mandado.
es.B: Así que bajó a la era e hizo exactamente lo que su suegra le había indicado.
es.R: Así que Rut bajó a la era e hizo tal como su suegra le había dicho.

fr.L: Et elle descendit à l’aire et fit selon tout ce que sa belle-mère lui avait ordonné.
fr.B: Elle descendit donc à l’aire et fit exactement ce que sa belle-mère lui avait recommandé.
fr.R: Ruth est donc descendue à l’aire, et elle a fait exactement ce que sa belle-mère lui avait dit.

vi.L: Vậy nàng đi xuống sân đập lúa và làm đúng mọi điều mẹ chồng đã dặn bảo nàng.
vi.B: Vậy nàng đi xuống sân đập lúa và làm đúng như mẹ chồng đã dặn.
vi.R: Vậy Ru-tơ đi xuống sân đập lúa và làm đúng như mẹ chồng đã bảo.

ko.L: 룻이 타작마당으로 내려가서 시어머니가 자기에게 명령한 대로 다 하였다.
ko.B: 그래서 룻은 타작마당으로 내려가서 시어머니가 일러 준 대로 그대로 하였다.
ko.R: 그래서 룻은 타작마당으로 내려가서 시어머니가 말한 대로 하였다.

pt.L: E ela desceu à eira e fez conforme tudo o que a sua sogra lhe tinha ordenado.
pt.B: Então ela desceu à eira e fez exatamente o que a sua sogra lhe tinha recomendado.
pt.R: Então Rute desceu até a eira e fez tudo o que a sogra lhe tinha mandado.

decisions.choice: did according to all: a summary told first
decisions.reason: The verse sums up what follows: verse 7 tells how she carried out each step. In fact she goes one step further than Naomi said, by speaking first (verse 9).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אכַל בֹּ֤עַז וַיֵּשְׁתְּ֙ וַיִּיטַ֣ב לִבּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕א לִשְׁכַּ֖ב בִּקְצֵ֣ה הָעֲרֵמָ֑ה וַתָּבֹ֣א בַלָּ֔ט וַתְּגַ֥ל מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וַתִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And ate Boaz and drank, and was good his heart, and he went to lie down at [the] end of the heap; and she came in secret and uncovered his feet and lay down.

en.L: And Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was good, and he went to lie down at the end of the grain heap. Then she came quietly and uncovered his feet and lay down.
en.B: Boaz ate and drank and was in a happy mood. He went off and lay down at the far end of the grain pile, and she came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
en.R: Boaz ate and drank, and he felt happy and content. Then he went to sleep at the far end of the pile of grain. Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet by turning back his cloak, and lay down there.

sw.L: Naye Boazi akala, akanywa, na moyo wake ukawa mwema, akaenda kulala mwisho wa lile rundo la nafaka. Naye akaja kimya kimya, akafunua miguu yake, akalala.
sw.B: Boazi alikula na kunywa, akachangamka. Alikwenda kulala upande wa mwisho wa rundo la nafaka, naye Ruthu akaja kimya kimya, akafunua miguu yake, akalala.
sw.R: Boazi alikula na kunywa, akajisikia mwenye furaha na kuridhika. Kisha alikwenda kulala upande wa mwisho wa rundo la nafaka. Ruthu alikuja kimya kimya, akafunua miguu yake kwa kulirudisha nyuma vazi lake, akalala hapo.

es.L: Y Booz comió y bebió, y su corazón estuvo alegre, y fue a acostarse al extremo del montón de grano. Y ella vino calladamente y descubrió sus pies y se acostó.
es.B: Booz comió y bebió y estaba de buen ánimo. Se fue a acostar al otro extremo del montón de grano, y ella llegó sin hacer ruido, le descubrió los pies y se acostó.
es.R: Booz comió y bebió, y se sentía feliz y contento. Después se fue a dormir al otro extremo del montón de grano. Rut llegó sin hacer ruido, le descubrió los pies apartando su manto y se acostó allí.

fr.L: Et Booz mangea et but, et son cœur fut content, et il alla se coucher au bout du tas [de grain]. Et elle vint doucement, découvrit ses pieds et se coucha.
fr.B: Booz mangea et but, et il était de bonne humeur. Il alla se coucher à l’autre bout du tas de grain, et elle vint sans bruit, découvrit ses pieds et se coucha.
fr.R: Booz a mangé et bu, et il était content et heureux. Ensuite, il est allé dormir à l’autre bout du tas de grain. Ruth est arrivée sans bruit, elle a découvert ses pieds en soulevant le bord de sa couverture, et elle s’est couchée là.

vi.L: Bô-ô ăn uống, lòng ông vui vẻ, và ông đi nằm ở cuối đống lúa. Rồi nàng đến lặng lẽ, giở chỗ chân ông ra và nằm xuống.
vi.B: Bô-ô ăn uống xong thì lòng thấy vui vẻ. Ông đến nằm ở đầu kia đống lúa. Nàng đến lặng lẽ, giở chăn nơi chân ông ra và nằm xuống.
vi.R: Bô-ô ăn uống xong, lòng thấy vui vẻ và mãn nguyện. Rồi ông đi ngủ ở đầu kia đống lúa. Ru-tơ đến lặng lẽ, lật tấm áo choàng nơi chân ông lên, và nằm xuống đó.

ko.L: 보아스가 먹고 마시고 마음이 즐거워져서, 곡식 더미 끝에 가서 누웠다. 그러자 룻이 살그머니 가서 그의 발치를 들추고 누웠다.
ko.B: 보아스는 먹고 마시고 기분이 좋아져서, 곡식 더미 끝으로 가서 누웠다. 그러자 룻이 살그머니 가서 그의 발치 이불을 들추고 누웠다.
ko.R: 보아스는 먹고 마시고 나서 기분이 좋았다. 그는 곡식 더미 끝으로 가서 잠자리에 들었다. 룻이 살그머니 다가가서 그의 겉옷을 젖혀 발을 드러내고 거기에 누웠다.

pt.L: E Boaz comeu e bebeu, e o seu coração ficou alegre, e ele foi se deitar na ponta do monte de grãos. Então ela veio às escondidas, e descobriu os pés dele, e se deitou.
pt.B: Boaz comeu e bebeu e ficou de bom humor. Ele foi se deitar na outra ponta do monte de grãos, e ela chegou sem fazer barulho, descobriu os pés dele e se deitou.
pt.R: Boaz comeu e bebeu e ficou alegre e satisfeito. Depois ele foi dormir na outra ponta do monte de grãos. Rute chegou de mansinho, descobriu os pés dele, dobrando para trás a capa dele, e se deitou ali.

decisions.choice: his heart was good: he was cheerful and content
decisions.reason: "His heart was good" means he was in good spirits after the meal (Judges 19:6; 1 Kings 21:7). It does not say he was drunk; the harvest meal ends a good day's work, and Boaz is clear-headed when he wakes (verses 10-13).

decisions.choice: at the end of the grain heap: guarding the harvest
decisions.reason: The owner slept beside the heap of winnowed grain to guard it through the night. The edge of the heap was away from the others, which let Ruth come to him unseen.

decisions.choice: quietly ... uncovered his feet
decisions.reason: The word means secretly or softly, without being noticed (1 Samuel 18:22; 24:5). She does just what Naomi said (verse 4); see the decision there on uncovering his feet.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד הָאִ֖ישׁ וַיִּלָּפֵ֑ת וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִשָּׁ֔ה שֹׁכֶ֖בֶת מַרְגְּלֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] middle of the night, and trembled the man and turned himself, and there, a woman lying [at] his feet.

en.L: And it happened at midnight that the man was startled and turned himself, and there was a woman lying at his feet!
en.B: In the middle of the night the man woke with a start and turned over. A woman was lying at his feet!
en.R: In the middle of the night Boaz suddenly woke up. He turned over and was surprised to find a woman lying at his feet.

sw.L: Ikawa usiku wa manane mtu huyo akashtuka, akajigeuza, na tazama, mwanamke amelala miguuni pake!
sw.B: Usiku wa manane mtu huyo aliamka kwa mshtuko, akajigeuza. Mwanamke alikuwa amelala miguuni pake!
sw.R: Usiku wa manane Boazi aliamka ghafla. Alijigeuza, akashangaa kumkuta mwanamke amelala miguuni pake.

es.L: Y sucedió a la medianoche que el hombre se sobresaltó y se volvió, ¡y he aquí una mujer acostada a sus pies!
es.B: A medianoche el hombre se despertó sobresaltado y se dio la vuelta. ¡Había una mujer acostada a sus pies!
es.R: A medianoche Booz se despertó de repente. Se dio la vuelta y se sorprendió al encontrar a una mujer acostada a sus pies.

fr.L: Et il arriva au milieu de la nuit que l’homme sursauta et se retourna, et voici, une femme était couchée à ses pieds !
fr.B: Au milieu de la nuit, l’homme se réveilla en sursaut et se retourna : une femme était couchée à ses pieds !
fr.R: Au milieu de la nuit, Booz s’est réveillé tout à coup. Il s’est retourné et il a été surpris de trouver une femme couchée à ses pieds.

vi.L: Vào nửa đêm, người ấy giật mình và trở mình, và kìa, có một người đàn bà nằm nơi chân ông!
vi.B: Nửa đêm, người ấy giật mình thức dậy và trở mình. Có một người đàn bà đang nằm nơi chân ông!
vi.R: Nửa đêm, Bô-ô bỗng thức giấc. Ông trở mình và ngạc nhiên thấy một người đàn bà đang nằm nơi chân mình.

ko.L: 한밤중에 그 사람이 놀라서 몸을 돌이켰는데, 보라, 한 여자가 그의 발치에 누워 있었다!
ko.B: 한밤중에 그 사람이 깜짝 놀라 깨어 몸을 뒤척였다. 한 여자가 그의 발치에 누워 있었다!
ko.R: 한밤중에 보아스가 갑자기 깨어났다. 그는 몸을 돌리다가 한 여자가 자기 발치에 누워 있는 것을 보고 깜짝 놀랐다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, à meia-noite, que o homem se assustou e se virou, e eis que uma mulher estava deitada aos seus pés!
pt.B: No meio da noite, o homem acordou assustado e se virou. Havia uma mulher deitada aos seus pés!
pt.R: No meio da noite, Boaz acordou de repente. Ele se virou e ficou surpreso ao ver uma mulher deitada aos seus pés.

decisions.choice: startled and turned himself: he woke with a start and turned or bent forward
alternatives: he bent forward (to feel what was there)
decisions.reason: The first verb means to tremble or start in fear or surprise. The second means to twist, turn or bend; Judges 16:29 uses it of Samson taking hold of the pillars. Boaz may have shivered with the cold at his uncovered feet, then turned over or leaned forward to see.

decisions.choice: there was a woman: seen through Boaz's eyes
decisions.reason: The word "there" (hinneh) takes the reader into Boaz's surprise. In the dark he sees only that a woman is lying there; he does not yet know who she is (verse 9).

decisions.choice: Boaz
decisions.reason: Readable names "the man" as Boaz, as verse 7 has.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־אָ֑תּוַתֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ ר֣וּת אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֤ כְנָפֶ֨ךָ֙ עַל־אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, who [are] you? And she said, I [am] Ruth your maidservant, and you will spread your wing over your maidservant, for a redeemer you [are].

en.L: And he said, "Who are you?" And she said, "I am Ruth, your maidservant. Spread your wing over your maidservant, for you are a redeemer."
en.B: "Who are you?" he asked. She answered, "I am Ruth, your servant. Spread the wing of your cloak over your servant, for you are a family redeemer."
en.R: "Who are you?" he asked. She answered, "I am Ruth, your servant. Cover me with the corner of your cloak to show that you will marry me and take care of me. You are one of our family redeemers."

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Wewe ni nani?" Naye akasema, "Mimi ni Ruthu, mjakazi wako. Utandaze bawa lako juu ya mjakazi wako, kwa maana wewe ni mkombozi."
sw.B: Akauliza, "Wewe ni nani?" Akajibu, "Mimi ni Ruthu, mtumishi wako. Tandaza upindo wa vazi lako juu ya mtumishi wako, kwa maana wewe ni mkombozi wa jamaa."
sw.R: Akauliza, "Wewe ni nani?" Akajibu, "Mimi ni Ruthu, mtumishi wako. Nifunike kwa pembe ya vazi lako kuonyesha kwamba utanioa na kunitunza. Wewe ni mmoja wa wakombozi wa jamaa yetu."

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Quién eres?». Y ella dijo: «Yo soy Rut, tu sierva. Extiende tu ala sobre tu sierva, porque tú eres redentor».
es.B: «¿Quién eres?», le preguntó. Ella respondió: «Soy Rut, tu sierva. Extiende el ala de tu manto sobre tu sierva, porque tú eres pariente redentor».
es.R: «¿Quién eres?», le preguntó. Ella le contestó: «Soy Rut, tu sierva. Cúbreme con el borde de tu manto, para mostrar que te casarás conmigo y me cuidarás. Tú eres uno de nuestros parientes redentores».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Qui es-tu ? » Et elle dit : « Je suis Ruth, ta servante. Étends ton aile sur ta servante, car tu es rédempteur. »
fr.B: « Qui es-tu ? » demanda-t-il. Elle répondit : « Je suis Ruth, ta servante. Étends sur ta servante l’aile de ton manteau, car tu es un proche parent rédempteur. »
fr.R: « Qui es-tu ? » a-t-il demandé. Elle a répondu : « Je suis Ruth, ta servante. Couvre-moi avec le bord de ton manteau, pour montrer que tu vas m’épouser et prendre soin de moi. Tu es l’un de nos proches parents rédempteurs. »

vi.L: Ông hỏi: "Ngươi là ai?" Nàng đáp: "Tôi là Ru-tơ, tớ gái của ông. Xin ông giăng cánh của ông trên tớ gái ông, vì ông là người chuộc lại."
vi.B: Ông hỏi: "Ai đó?" Nàng đáp: "Tôi là Ru-tơ, đầy tớ gái của ông. Xin ông giăng cánh áo của ông che cho đầy tớ gái ông, vì ông là người bà con có quyền chuộc lại."
vi.R: Ông hỏi: "Ai đó?" Nàng trả lời: "Tôi là Ru-tơ, đầy tớ của ông. Xin ông lấy vạt áo choàng của ông che cho tôi, để tỏ rằng ông sẽ cưới tôi và chăm sóc tôi. Ông là một trong những người bà con có quyền chuộc lại của gia đình chúng tôi."

pt.R: "Quem é você?", ele perguntou. Ela respondeu: "Eu sou Rute, a sua serva. Cubra-me com a aba da sua capa, para mostrar que o senhor vai se casar comigo e cuidar de mim. O senhor é um dos resgatadores da nossa família."

decisions.choice: spread your wing over: take me as your wife and under your protection
decisions.reason: The word means a wing, and also the corner or edge of a garment. Spreading the corner of one's garment over a woman was a sign of taking her as wife (Ezekiel 16:8, where God says "I spread my wing over you ... and you became mine"; compare Deuteronomy 23:1). Boaz had prayed that Ruth would find a full reward from the LORD, "under whose wings you have come to take refuge" (2:12). Now she asks Boaz himself to be the answer to that prayer.

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a woman who could become a wife
decisions.reason: In 2:13 Ruth called herself by a humbler word for a servant girl, one not even counted among his servants. Here she uses another word for a female servant, one used of women who could be taken as wives (as Hagar and Bilhah, Genesis 21:10; 30:3). She speaks humbly, but as one who may marry him.

decisions.choice: you are a redeemer: the reason for her request
decisions.reason: The redeemer (go'el) was the close relative bound to buy back family land and care for the family line (2:20; Leviticus 25:25). The law gave the duty of marrying a dead man's widow to his brother (Deuteronomy 25:5-10), not to the redeemer. Ruth joins the two duties: she asks Boaz, as redeemer, to marry her and keep her dead husband's family alive. Boaz accepts that this goes together (verses 12-13), and so does the town (4:5, 10).

decisions.choice: the wing of your cloak
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the word "wing", so that the link with 2:12 can be seen, and adds "of your cloak" to show that a garment is meant. Literal keeps "your wing" alone.

decisions.choice: to show that you will marry me and take care of me ... one of our family redeemers
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant (decision m1) and names the family the redeemer acts for (decision m3). It says "one of our family redeemers", as Naomi did (2:20), because a nearer redeemer exists (verse 12).

decisions.choice: family redeemer
decisions.reason: "Family redeemer" at Balanced and Readable, "redeemer" at Literal, as throughout Ruth (2:20), so that the reader sees a relative's duty is meant, not salvation from sin.

decisions.choice: "bawa" (wing) at Literal, "upindo wa vazi" (the edge of the cloak) at Balanced
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the same as the "wings" of the LORD in 2:12 (m1). Literal keeps "bawa", so that the link with "mabawa" in 2:12 can be seen; Balanced names the cloak, as the English "the wing of your cloak" does, and Readable says what the act means.

decisions.choice: "extiende tu ala" (L); "extiende el ala de tu manto" (B); "cúbreme con el borde de tu manto" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means both a wing and the corner of a garment. Literal and Balanced keep "ala", so that the reader hears Boaz's own blessing in 2:12, "bajo cuyas alas": Ruth asks Boaz to be the shelter he prayed God would give her (m1). Readable says what the gesture means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ton aile" (L); "l'aile de ton manteau" (B); "le bord de ton manteau" (R)
alternatives: "le pan de ton manteau" at Balanced, which loses the link with 2:12
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means both a wing and the corner of a garment (m1). Boaz blessed Ruth for taking refuge under the LORD's "wings" (2:12), and now she asks him to spread his own "wing" over her. Literal and Balanced keep "aile" so the reader can see the link, as the terms note asks; Readable says what the gesture meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "giăng cánh" (L), "giăng cánh áo" (B) for "spread your wing"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "wing" is also the corner of a cloak, and it takes up Boaz's blessing in 2:12, "dưới cánh" (meaning decision). Vietnamese "cánh áo", the flap of a garment, keeps the same word at Balanced; Readable says what the gesture means.

decisions.choice: Boaz, startled in the dark, says "ngươi" at Literal; Balanced and Readable "Ai đó?"
decisions.reason: He does not yet know who is there; a bare "Who are you?" needs a pronoun in Vietnamese, and "ngươi" is the neutral one for an unknown person at Literal. The other levels avoid the pronoun.

decisions.choice: "날개" kept at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the "wing" under which Ruth came to shelter in 2:12, here the corner of Boaz's cloak. Keeping "날개" lets the reader hear the link; Readable says what the gesture asks.

decisions.choice: "기업 무를 자" at Literal; "집안을 책임지는 친족" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for *goel*, and as 2:20.

decisions.choice: Estenda a sua asa (L); Estenda ... a aba do seu manto (B); Cubra-me com a aba da sua capa (R)
alternatives: Estenda a asa do seu manto
decisions.reason: Kanaf is both a wing and the corner of a garment (m1). Literal keeps "asa", so that Ruth's words echo Boaz's prayer that she find refuge under the LORD's "asas" (2:12). Portuguese cannot say "a asa do manto", so Balanced and Readable say "a aba", the flap or edge of a garment, the other sense of the same word, and the meaning note keeps the link; Readable adds what the gesture meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: a sua serva; o senhor
decisions.reason: Ruth speaks of herself as "a sua serva" ('amah, a servant who could become a wife, m2) and to Boaz as "o senhor", the address of section 4 for a superior, as in 2:10, 13. 'Amah is "serva" at every level, kept apart from "criada" for shifchah in 2:13 at Literal.

records.literal_gloss: And he said, blessed [are] you by YHWH, my daughter; you have made good your latter steadfast love more than the first, by not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.

en.B: He said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, my daughter! This faithful love you have shown now is greater than what you showed before, since you have not looked to the young men for a husband, whether poor or rich.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyalty and kindness beyond what duty asks
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) means loyal, faithful love, kindness that keeps faith with those one is bound to and goes beyond what is owed. It is the word Naomi used when she prayed for her daughters-in-law (1:8) and the word for the LORD's love in Exodus 34:6.

decisions.choice: the latter better than the first: two acts of loyalty
alternatives: the first: her kindness to her dead husband (1:8)
decisions.reason: The first act of faithful love is most likely Ruth's leaving her own land to care for Naomi (2:11; 1:16-17). The latter is this night's request: instead of choosing a husband for herself, she has asked the family's redeemer to marry her, so that her dead husband's name and Naomi's family line may go on (4:10).

decisions.choice: not going after the young men: not looking for a husband of her own age
decisions.reason: "Going after" a man means seeking him as a husband. Boaz's words suggest he is older than Ruth. "Whether poor or rich" means any young man at all: she was free to look for love or for wealth, and chose family loyalty instead.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is rendered as in Exodus 34:6 and Deuteronomy: "steadfast love" at Literal, "faithful love" at Balanced and Readable, which shows both the loyalty and the warmth of the word.

decisions.choice: to Naomi before
decisions.reason: Readable names Naomi as the one Ruth first showed faithful love to (decision m2), and puts "going after the young men" as trying to marry a younger man (decision m3).

decisions.choice: looked to the young men for a husband
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "going after" the young men means (decision m3).

decisions.choice: "fadhili" for chesed here, between people
decisions.reason: As agreed for Ruth: here chesed is Ruth's loyal kindness to her family and to Boaz, and "fadhili" is the Swahili word for kindness shown between people; 1:8 and 2:20, where the LORD's love is spoken of, keep "upendo usiokoma".

decisions.choice: "lòng nhân từ" for Ruth's *hesed*
decisions.reason: The Joshua–Ruth terms note gives "lòng nhân từ" for *hesed* between people. At 1:8 the same word was given as "tình yêu thương thành tín" because one sentence joins the LORD's love and the daughters-in-law's; here it is Ruth's alone. A reviewer may prefer one word for both places.

decisions.choice: "한결같은 사랑" (Readable "변함없는 사랑") for Ruth's *hesed*
decisions.reason: The same words as in 1:8 and 2:20, so that the reader sees the book's key word come back, now said of Ruth.

decisions.choice: lealdade (L); bondade leal (B); bondosa e leal (R)
decisions.reason: Here chesed (m1) is Ruth's, shown to her family, so it takes the wording set for chesed between people in Joshua 2:12 and in 1:8 of this book: "lealdade" at Literal, "bondade leal" at Balanced, "bondosa e leal" at Readable. "Amor" would suggest romance in a scene where Boaz praises her loyalty, not her feeling for him.

decisions.choice: all the gate of my people: everyone in the town
decisions.reason: The gate of a town was where its people met, where business was done and where the elders settled cases (4:1, 11). "All the gate of my people" means the whole town, all who gather there.

decisions.choice: a woman of worth: strong, capable and good
decisions.reason: The phrase (eshet chayil) joins "woman" with a word for strength, ability and worth. It is the phrase of Proverbs 31:10 and 12:4. The same word chayil described Boaz, "a man mighty in wealth" (2:1): Ruth is his equal in character, though she is a poor foreigner.

decisions.choice: all that you say I will do for you
decisions.reason: Boaz answers Ruth with the very words she gave Naomi (verse 5).

decisions.choice: ask
decisions.reason: "Say" here means what Ruth has asked of him, so Balanced and Readable say "ask". Literal keeps "say" to show the echo of verse 5.

decisions.choice: "성문에 있는 모든 사람" (all the gate of my people) at Literal
decisions.reason: The town gate was where the people met and judged; Literal keeps the picture, and Balanced and Readable say "the town".

decisions.choice: uma mulher de valor (L); uma mulher virtuosa, de valor (B); uma mulher virtuosa e de bom caráter (R)
decisions.reason: Chayil is the word used of Boaz in 2:1, "um homem de valor" (m2). Literal says "uma mulher de valor" so the two match word for word; Balanced keeps "de valor" beside "virtuosa", the word Brazilian readers know from Proverbs 31:10, and Readable says "virtuosa e de bom caráter", as the English Readable says "of good character".

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ כִּ֣י אָמְנָ֔ם כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי וְגַ֛ם יֵ֥שׁ גֹּאֵ֖ל קָר֥וֹב מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, truly that [if] a redeemer I [am], and also there is a redeemer nearer than I.

en.L: And now, truly I am a redeemer; and yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.
en.B: It is true that I am a family redeemer, but there is a family redeemer more closely related than I am.
en.R: It is true that I am a family redeemer. But there is another man who is a closer relative than I am, and he has the first right to redeem you.

sw.L: Na sasa, ni kweli kwamba mimi ni mkombozi; lakini yuko mkombozi aliye karibu zaidi kuliko mimi.
sw.B: Ni kweli kwamba mimi ni mkombozi wa jamaa, lakini yuko mkombozi wa jamaa aliye ndugu wa karibu zaidi kuliko mimi.
sw.R: Ni kweli kwamba mimi ni mkombozi wa jamaa. Lakini yuko mtu mwingine aliye jamaa wa karibu zaidi kuliko mimi, naye ana haki ya kwanza ya kukukomboa.

es.L: Y ahora, es verdad que yo soy redentor; pero también hay un redentor más cercano que yo.
es.B: Es verdad que soy pariente redentor, pero hay otro pariente redentor más cercano que yo.
es.R: Es verdad que soy pariente redentor. Pero hay otro hombre que es pariente más cercano que yo, y él tiene el primer derecho de redimirte.

fr.L: Et maintenant, il est vrai que je suis rédempteur ; mais il y a aussi un rédempteur plus proche que moi.
fr.B: Il est vrai que je suis un proche parent rédempteur, mais il y en a un autre plus proche que moi.
fr.R: C’est vrai, je suis un proche parent rédempteur. Mais il y a un autre homme qui est un parent plus proche que moi, et c’est lui qui a le droit de te racheter en premier.

vi.L: Bây giờ, thật ta là người chuộc lại; nhưng còn có một người chuộc lại gần hơn ta.
vi.B: Đúng là ta là người bà con có quyền chuộc lại, nhưng còn có một người bà con có quyền chuộc lại gần hơn ta.
vi.R: Đúng là ta là người bà con có quyền chuộc lại. Nhưng có một người khác là bà con gần hơn ta, và người ấy có quyền chuộc lại con trước.

ko.L: 이제 내가 기업 무를 자인 것은 사실이다. 그러나 나보다 더 가까운 기업 무를 자가 있다.
ko.B: 내가 너희 집안을 책임지는 친족인 것은 사실이다. 그러나 나보다 더 가까운 친족이 있다.
ko.R: 내가 너희 집안을 책임지는 친족인 것은 맞다. 그러나 나보다 더 가까운 친척이 한 사람 있다. 그 사람에게 너를 맡을 첫째 권리가 있다.

pt.L: E agora, é verdade que eu sou resgatador; mas há ainda um resgatador mais próximo do que eu.
pt.B: É verdade que eu sou um resgatador da família, mas há um resgatador que é parente mais próximo do que eu.
pt.R: É verdade que eu sou um resgatador da família. Mas há outro homem que é parente mais próximo do que eu, e ele tem o direito de resgatar você primeiro.

decisions.choice: it is true that: a written word is left unread
alternatives: truly, if I am a redeemer (with the written word)
decisions.reason: After "that" the written text (ketiv) has a further word, "if", which the reading tradition (qere) tells the reader to leave out. Read with it, the words would be an unusual way of saying "truly that"; read without it, "it is true that". The sense is the same, and the reading tradition is followed.

decisions.choice: a redeemer nearer than I: the closer relative has the first right
decisions.reason: The duty and right to redeem passed to the nearest relative first, and then to the next (Leviticus 25:25, 48-49). Boaz is willing, but he will not set aside the right of the closer relative; chapter 4 tells how the matter is settled at the town gate (4:1-10).

decisions.choice: and he has the first right to redeem you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "nearer" means for Ruth (decision m2).

source.text: לִ֣ינִי׀הַלַּ֗יְלָה וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ אִם־יִגְאָלֵ֥ךְ טוֹב֙ יִגְאָ֔ל וְאִם־לֹ֨א יַחְפֹּ֧ץ לְגָֽאֳלֵ֛ךְ וּגְאַלְתִּ֥יךְ אָנֹ֖כִי חַי־יְהוָ֑ה שִׁכְבִ֖י עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Stay the night, and it will be in the morning, if he will redeem you, good, let him redeem; and if he is not willing to redeem you, then I will redeem you, I, [as] YHWH lives. Lie down until the morning.

en.L: Stay the night, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good, let him redeem; but if he is not willing to redeem you, then I will redeem you, I myself, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives. Lie down until the morning."
en.B: Stay here for the night. In the morning, if he will act as redeemer for you, well and good: let him do it. But if he does not want to redeem you, then as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, I will redeem you myself. Lie down here until morning."
en.R: Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he is willing to redeem you, that is fine; let him do it. But if he does not want to, then I promise you, as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, I will do it myself. Now lie down here until morning."

sw.L: Kaa usiku huu, na asubuhi, kama atakukomboa, vema, na akomboe; lakini kama hataki kukukomboa, basi nitakukomboa mimi, mimi mwenyewe, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo. Lala mpaka asubuhi."
sw.B: Kaa hapa usiku huu. Asubuhi, kama atakuwa mkombozi wako, vema, na afanye hivyo. Lakini kama hataki kukukomboa, basi hakika kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, nitakukomboa mimi mwenyewe. Lala hapa mpaka asubuhi."
sw.R: Kaa hapa usiku huu. Asubuhi, kama yuko tayari kukukomboa, ni sawa; na afanye hivyo. Lakini kama hataki, basi nakuahidi, hakika kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, nitafanya hivyo mimi mwenyewe. Sasa lala hapa mpaka asubuhi."

es.L: Pasa la noche, y será que por la mañana, si él te redime, bien, que redima; pero si no quiere redimirte, entonces te redimiré yo, yo mismo, ¡vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! Acuéstate hasta la mañana».
es.B: Quédate aquí esta noche. Por la mañana, si él quiere hacer contigo de redentor, muy bien, que lo haga. Pero si no quiere redimirte, entonces, tan cierto como que vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, yo mismo te redimiré. Acuéstate aquí hasta la mañana».
es.R: Quédate aquí esta noche. Por la mañana, si él está dispuesto a redimirte, está bien; que lo haga. Pero si no quiere, entonces te lo prometo, tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive: lo haré yo mismo. Ahora acuéstate aquí hasta la mañana».

fr.L: Passe la nuit ici, et au matin, s’il veut te racheter, bien, qu’il rachète ; mais s’il ne veut pas te racheter, c’est moi qui te rachèterai, moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant ! Couche-toi jusqu’au matin. »
fr.B: Reste ici cette nuit. Demain matin, s’il veut jouer pour toi le rôle de rédempteur, très bien, qu’il le fasse. Mais s’il ne veut pas te racheter, aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, je te rachèterai moi-même. Couche-toi ici jusqu’au matin. »
fr.R: Reste ici cette nuit. Demain matin, s’il veut te racheter, c’est bien, qu’il le fasse. Mais s’il ne veut pas, je te le promets, aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, je le ferai moi-même. Maintenant, couche-toi ici jusqu’au matin. »

vi.L: Đêm nay hãy ở lại; sáng mai, nếu người ấy chuộc con, tốt, cứ để người ấy chuộc; còn nếu người ấy không muốn chuộc con, thì ta sẽ chuộc con, chính ta, [ta chỉ] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống [mà thề]. Hãy nằm cho đến sáng."
vi.B: Đêm nay con hãy ở lại đây. Sáng mai, nếu người ấy chịu làm người chuộc lại cho con thì tốt, cứ để người ấy làm. Nhưng nếu người ấy không muốn chuộc con, thì ta chỉ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống mà thề, chính ta sẽ chuộc con. Con cứ nằm đây cho đến sáng."
vi.R: Đêm nay con hãy ở lại đây. Sáng mai, nếu người ấy muốn chuộc con thì tốt, cứ để người ấy làm. Nhưng nếu người ấy không muốn, thì ta hứa với con, ta chỉ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống mà thề, chính ta sẽ làm việc ấy. Bây giờ con cứ nằm đây cho đến sáng."

ko.L: 오늘 밤은 여기에서 지내라. 아침에 그가 너를 맡아 기업을 무르겠다고 하면 좋다, 그가 무르게 하여라. 그러나 그가 너를 맡아 기업을 무르려 하지 않으면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 두고 말하는데, 내가 너를 맡겠다. 아침까지 누워 있어라."
ko.B: 오늘 밤은 여기에서 지내라. 아침에 그가 너를 맡겠다고 하면 좋다. 그가 맡게 하자. 그러나 그가 너를 맡으려 하지 않으면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데, 내가 너를 맡겠다. 아침까지 여기 누워 있어라."
ko.R: 오늘 밤은 여기에서 지내라. 아침에 그가 너를 맡겠다고 하면 좋다. 그가 맡게 하자. 그러나 그가 원하지 않으면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 두고 약속하는데, 내가 너를 맡겠다. 이제 아침까지 여기 누워 있어라."

pt.L: Passe a noite [aqui], e pela manhã, se ele a resgatar, bem, que resgate; mas, se ele não quiser resgatá-la, eu a resgatarei, eu, pela vida {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Deite-se até de manhã."
pt.B: Passe a noite aqui. De manhã, se ele quiser cumprir para você o papel de resgatador, muito bem, que o cumpra. Mas, se ele não quiser resgatá-la, tão certo como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive, eu mesmo a resgatarei. Deite-se aqui até de manhã."
pt.R: Fique aqui esta noite. De manhã, se ele quiser resgatar você, tudo bem; que ele faça isso. Mas, se ele não quiser, então eu prometo a você, tão certo como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive, que eu mesmo vou fazer isso. Agora deite-se aqui até de manhã."

decisions.choice: redeem you: take responsibility for you and your family's land and line
decisions.reason: Here "redeem" means more than buying land: it means taking Ruth as wife and caring for Elimelech's family, its land and its name, as chapter 4 shows (4:5, 10).

decisions.choice: as the LORD lives: an oath
decisions.reason: Boaz binds himself with an oath by the life of the LORD. He does not leave Ruth with a vague hope: if the nearer relative will not act, Boaz will.

decisions.choice: stay the night ... lie down until the morning: for her safety
decisions.reason: Boaz does not send Ruth home through the dark, where she could be harmed or seen (compare 2:22). She is to stay where she is until it is nearly light (verse 14).

decisions.choice: good, let him redeem
decisions.reason: The word means "good": that would be well. It is not a name, though some have read it as one ("if Tob will redeem you").

decisions.choice: act as redeemer for you
decisions.reason: Balanced says "act as redeemer for you" the first time, so the reader takes "redeem" as a relative's duty (decision m1); after that it says "redeem".

decisions.choice: "racheter" for the verb, matching "rédempteur" for the noun
decisions.reason: French has no everyday verb from "rédempteur"; "racheter" is the word for buying back what belonged to the family, and it says what the redeemer does (m1). It is used for the verb through chapters 3 and 4.

decisions.choice: cumprir para você o papel de resgatador
decisions.reason: As the English Balanced does, the first use says what redeeming means here (m1), the duty of the resgatador of 2:20; after that Balanced says "resgatar", the verb of Leviticus 25:25 in Portuguese.

source.text: וַתִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מַרְגְּלוֹתָיוֹ֙עַד־הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֕קָם בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכִּ֥יר אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַל־יִוָּדַ֔ע כִּי־בָ֥אָה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַגֹּֽרֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And she lay [at] his feet until the morning, and she rose before could recognize a man his neighbor; and he said, let it not be known that came the woman [to] the threshing floor.

en.L: And she lay at his feet until morning, and she rose while it was still too early for one to recognize another. And he said, "May it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
en.B: So she lay at his feet until morning, but she got up before it was light enough for anyone to recognize another. And he said, "It must not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
en.R: So Ruth lay at his feet until morning. She got up while it was still too dark for people to see who anyone was. Boaz said, "No one must find out that a woman came to the threshing floor."

sw.L: Naye akalala miguuni pake mpaka asubuhi, akaamka kabla mtu hajaweza kumtambua mwenzake. Naye akasema, "Isijulikane ya kuwa mwanamke alikuja uwanjani pa kupuria."
sw.B: Basi alilala miguuni pake mpaka asubuhi, lakini aliamka kabla hakujawa na mwanga wa kutosha mtu kumtambua mwenzake. Naye akasema, "Isijulikane kwamba mwanamke alikuja uwanjani pa kupuria."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Ruthu alilala miguuni pake mpaka asubuhi. Aliamka kukiwa bado na giza mno watu wasiweze kutambuana. Boazi alisema, "Mtu yeyote asijue kwamba mwanamke alikuja uwanjani pa kupuria."

es.L: Y ella durmió a sus pies hasta la mañana, y se levantó antes de que uno pudiera reconocer a otro. Y él dijo: «Que no se sepa que la mujer vino a la era».
es.B: Así que ella se quedó acostada a sus pies hasta la mañana, pero se levantó antes de que hubiera luz suficiente para que nadie reconociera a nadie. Y él dijo: «No se debe saber que la mujer vino a la era».
es.R: Así que Rut se quedó acostada a sus pies hasta la mañana. Se levantó cuando todavía estaba tan oscuro que nadie podía ver quién era quién. Booz dijo: «Nadie debe enterarse de que una mujer vino a la era».

fr.L: Et elle resta couchée à ses pieds jusqu’au matin, et elle se leva avant qu’on puisse reconnaître son prochain. Et il dit : « Qu’on ne sache pas que la femme est venue à l’aire. »
fr.B: Elle resta donc couchée à ses pieds jusqu’au matin, mais elle se leva avant qu’il fasse assez jour pour qu’on puisse se reconnaître. Et il dit : « Il ne faut pas qu’on sache que cette femme est venue à l’aire. »
fr.R: Ruth est donc restée couchée à ses pieds jusqu’au matin. Elle s’est levée quand il faisait encore trop sombre pour qu’on puisse reconnaître les gens. Booz a dit : « Personne ne doit savoir qu’une femme est venue à l’aire. »

vi.L: Nàng nằm nơi chân ông cho đến sáng, rồi dậy trước khi người ta có thể nhận ra nhau. Ông nói: "Đừng để ai biết người đàn bà đã đến sân đập lúa."
vi.B: Vậy nàng nằm nơi chân ông cho đến sáng, nhưng dậy trước khi trời đủ sáng để người ta nhận ra nhau. Ông nói: "Không ai được biết có người đàn bà đã đến sân đập lúa."
vi.R: Vậy Ru-tơ nằm nơi chân ông cho đến sáng. Nàng dậy khi trời còn tối, chưa ai nhận ra được ai. Bô-ô nói: "Không ai được biết có người đàn bà đã đến sân đập lúa."

ko.L: 룻은 아침까지 그의 발치에 누워 있다가, 사람이 서로 알아볼 수 없을 만큼 이른 때에 일어났다. 보아스가 말했다. "여자가 타작마당에 왔다는 것을 아무도 몰라야 한다."
ko.B: 그래서 룻은 아침까지 그의 발치에 누워 있다가, 날이 밝아 사람을 알아볼 수 있기 전에 일어났다. 보아스가 말했다. "여자가 타작마당에 왔다는 것을 아무도 알아서는 안 된다."
ko.R: 그래서 룻은 아침까지 그의 발치에 누워 있었다. 룻은 아직 어두워서 사람들이 서로 누구인지 알아볼 수 없을 때에 일어났다. 보아스가 말했다. "여자가 타작마당에 왔다는 것을 아무도 알면 안 된다."

pt.L: E ela ficou deitada aos pés dele até de manhã, e se levantou antes que uma pessoa pudesse reconhecer outra. E ele disse: "Que não se saiba que a mulher veio à eira."
pt.B: Assim ela ficou deitada aos pés dele até de manhã, mas se levantou antes que houvesse luz para alguém reconhecer outra pessoa. E ele disse: "Ninguém pode saber que a mulher veio à eira."
pt.R: Assim Rute ficou deitada aos pés de Boaz até de manhã. Ela se levantou quando ainda estava escuro demais para alguém reconhecer quem era quem. Boaz disse: "Ninguém pode descobrir que uma mulher veio à eira."

decisions.choice: his feet; before: the readings of the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) are two spellings of the same words, "his feet" and "before". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: let it not be known: to guard her name
decisions.reason: A woman found at night at a threshing floor would be suspected of selling herself, since harvest time and threshing floors were linked with that (Hosea 9:1). Boaz protects Ruth's good name, and keeps the matter quiet until it is settled with the nearer redeemer.

decisions.choice: he said: to Ruth, or to himself
decisions.reason: The verse does not say whom Boaz spoke to. He may have said it to Ruth as she left, or to himself, as "said" can mean thought (Genesis 20:11). The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: one ... another / anyone ... another / anyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a man his neighbor", an idiom for one person and another; it is not about men only. Every level says so in words that are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: Boaz
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָ֠בִי הַמִּטְפַּ֧חַת אֲשֶׁר־עָלַ֛יִךְ וְאֶֽחֳזִי־בָ֖הּ וַתֹּ֣אחֶז בָּ֑הּ וַיָּ֤מָד שֵׁשׁ־שְׂעֹרִים֙ וַיָּ֣שֶׁת עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיָּבֹ֖א הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, bring the shawl that [is] on you and hold it; and she held it, and he measured six [of] barley and put [it] on her; and he went [into] the city.

en.L: And he said, "Give [me] the shawl that is on you, and take hold of it." And she took hold of it, and he measured six [measures of] barley and laid [it] on her. Then he went into the town.
en.B: Then he said, "Hand me the shawl you have on and hold it out." When she held it out, he measured six measures of barley into it and set the load on her. Then he went into the town.
en.R: Boaz said, "Bring me the shawl you are wearing and hold it open." She held it open, and he poured six measures of barley into it and put the load on her to carry. Then Boaz went back to town.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Lete mtandio ulio juu yako, uushike." Naye akaushika, naye akapima [vipimo] sita vya shayiri, akamtwika. Kisha akaenda mjini.
sw.B: Kisha akasema, "Nipe mtandio ulioujifunika, uunyooshe." Alipounyoosha, alimpimia vipimo sita vya shayiri ndani yake, akamtwika mzigo huo. Kisha akaenda mjini.
sw.R: Boazi alisema, "Niletee mtandio uliojifunika, uushike wazi." Aliushika wazi, naye akamimina vipimo sita vya shayiri ndani yake, akamtwika mzigo huo aubebe. Kisha Boazi akarudi mjini.

es.L: Y dijo: «Dame el manto que [llevas] sobre ti, y sujétalo». Y ella lo sujetó, y él midió seis [medidas de] cebada y [se las] puso encima. Luego él se fue a la ciudad.
es.B: Luego le dijo: «Dame el manto que llevas puesto y sostenlo extendido». Cuando ella lo sostuvo, él le echó seis medidas de cebada y le puso la carga encima. Luego se fue al pueblo.
es.R: Booz le dijo: «Tráeme el manto que llevas puesto y sostenlo abierto». Ella lo sostuvo abierto, y él echó en él seis medidas de cebada y le puso la carga para que la llevara. Después Booz volvió al pueblo.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Donne le châle qui est sur toi, et tiens-le. » Et elle le tint, et il mesura six [mesures d’] orge et [les] posa sur elle. Puis il rentra dans la ville.
fr.B: Puis il lui dit : « Donne-moi le châle que tu portes, et tiens-le ouvert. » Quand elle le tint ouvert, il y versa six mesures d’orge et lui chargea le tout sur le dos. Puis il rentra en ville.
fr.R: Booz a dit : « Apporte-moi le châle que tu portes, et tiens-le ouvert. » Elle l’a tenu ouvert, et il y a versé six mesures d’orge. Il a mis la charge sur son dos pour qu’elle la porte. Ensuite, Booz est rentré en ville.

vi.L: Ông nói: "Hãy đưa cái khăn choàng con đang mang và giữ lấy nó." Nàng giữ nó, và ông đong sáu [đấu] lúa mạch đổ vào rồi đặt lên vai nàng. Rồi ông đi vào thành.
vi.B: Rồi ông nói: "Hãy đưa khăn choàng con đang mang mà căng ra." Nàng căng khăn ra, và ông đong sáu đấu lúa mạch đổ vào, rồi đặt lên vai nàng. Sau đó ông đi vào thành.
vi.R: Bô-ô nói: "Hãy đưa khăn choàng con đang mang và căng ra." Nàng căng khăn ra, và ông đổ sáu đấu lúa mạch vào đó, rồi đặt lên vai cho nàng mang. Rồi Bô-ô trở vào thành.

ko.L: 보아스가 말했다. "네가 두른 겉옷을 가져와서 붙잡고 있어라." 룻이 그것을 붙잡자, 그가 보리를 여섯 [번] 되어 룻에게 지워 주었다. 그리고 그는 성읍으로 들어갔다.
ko.B: 그리고 그가 말했다. "네가 두른 겉옷을 이리 가져와서 펴서 잡고 있어라." 룻이 그것을 펴서 잡자, 보아스는 보리를 여섯 번 되어 담아 주고 그 짐을 룻에게 지워 주었다. 그리고 그는 성읍으로 들어갔다.
ko.R: 보아스가 말했다. "네가 두른 겉옷을 가져와서 펴서 잡고 있어라." 룻이 겉옷을 펴서 잡자, 보아스는 보리를 여섯 번 되어 부어 주고 룻이 지고 가게 해 주었다. 그리고 보아스는 성으로 돌아갔다.

pt.L: E ele disse: "Dê [cá] o xale que está sobre você e segure-o." E ela o segurou, e ele mediu seis [medidas] de cevada e [as] pôs sobre ela. Então ele foi para a cidade.
pt.B: Depois ele disse: "Passe-me o xale que você está usando e segure-o aberto." Quando ela o segurou, ele mediu seis medidas de cevada, despejou no xale e pôs a carga sobre ela. Depois ele foi para a cidade.
pt.R: Boaz disse: "Traga o xale que você está usando e segure-o aberto." Ela o segurou aberto, e ele despejou nele seis medidas de cevada e pôs a carga sobre ela para ela levar. Depois Boaz voltou para a cidade.

decisions.choice: six of barley: six measures of an unnamed size
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "six of barley" and does not name the measure. Six ephahs (about 120 quarts) would be far too much for one woman to carry; six seahs (a seah is a third of an ephah) would still be very heavy. The measure may have been a smaller scoop or the like. All that is certain is that it was a generous gift that Ruth could carry.

decisions.choice: shawl: a wide cloak or wrap
decisions.reason: The word names a large wrap or mantle worn by women (Isaiah 3:22). Held out, it could hold a heavy load of grain.

decisions.choice: he went into the town: the received text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text says "he went", that is Boaz went into the town. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "she went", which fits the next verse, where Ruth comes to Naomi. The received text is followed; both are true in the story, since Boaz goes to the town gate (4:1) and Ruth goes home.

decisions.choice: six [measures of] barley / six measures of barley
decisions.reason: English needs a word for the unit, so "measures" is supplied (in brackets at Literal). No modern measure is given, since the Hebrew does not say which unit is meant (decision m1).

decisions.choice: town
decisions.reason: The word can mean a city or a town; Bethlehem was a small town, so every level says "town", as in 1:19 and 2:18.

decisions.choice: "sáu đấu" for "six [measures]"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name the measure (meaning decision); "đấu" is a plain Vietnamese word for a grain measure, used without a units span, as the English uses "measures".

decisions.choice: "여섯 번 되어" (measured six times)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name the measure; Korean says Boaz measured the barley out six times, which keeps the number without naming a unit.

decisions.choice: o xale
decisions.reason: The woman's wide wrap (m2) is "o xale", an everyday word, and it keeps her garment apart from Boaz's "manto" or "capa" of 3:9.

source.text: וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־חֲמוֹתָ֔הּ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־אַ֣תְּ בִּתִּ֑י וַתַּ֨גֶּד־לָ֔הּ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָֽשָׂה־לָ֖הּ הָאִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she came to her mother-in-law, and she said, who [are] you, my daughter? And she told her all that had done for her the man.

en.L: And she came to her mother-in-law, and she said, "Who are you, my daughter?" And she told her all that the man had done for her.
en.B: When she came to her mother-in-law, Naomi said, "How do things stand with you, my daughter?" Then Ruth told her everything the man had done for her.
en.R: When Ruth came home, her mother-in-law asked, "My daughter, how are things for you now?" Then Ruth told her everything that Boaz had done for her.

sw.L: Naye akafika kwa mama mkwe wake, naye akasema, "Wewe ni nani, binti yangu?" Naye akamweleza yote ambayo mtu yule alimtendea.
sw.B: Alipofika kwa mama mkwe wake, Naomi alimwuliza, "Mambo yako yamekuwaje, binti yangu?" Basi Ruthu alimweleza yote ambayo mtu yule alimtendea.
sw.R: Ruthu alipofika nyumbani, mama mkwe wake alimwuliza, "Binti yangu, hali yako ikoje sasa?" Kisha Ruthu alimweleza yote ambayo Boazi alimtendea.

es.L: Y ella llegó a su suegra, y esta dijo: «¿Quién eres, hija mía?». Y ella le contó todo lo que el hombre había hecho por ella.
es.B: Cuando llegó adonde estaba su suegra, Noemí le preguntó: «¿Cómo te ha ido, hija mía?». Entonces Rut le contó todo lo que el hombre había hecho por ella.
es.R: Cuando Rut llegó a casa, su suegra le preguntó: «Hija mía, ¿cómo te ha ido?». Entonces Rut le contó todo lo que Booz había hecho por ella.

fr.L: Et elle vint vers sa belle-mère, et celle-ci dit : « Qui es-tu, ma fille ? » Et elle lui raconta tout ce que l’homme avait fait pour elle.
fr.B: Quand elle arriva chez sa belle-mère, Noémi lui demanda : « Où en es-tu, ma fille ? » Ruth lui raconta alors tout ce que l’homme avait fait pour elle.
fr.R: Quand Ruth est rentrée à la maison, sa belle-mère lui a demandé : « Ma fille, comment ça s’est passé pour toi ? » Alors Ruth lui a raconté tout ce que Booz avait fait pour elle.

vi.L: Nàng đến với mẹ chồng, và bà hỏi: "Con là ai, con gái của mẹ?" Nàng kể cho bà mọi điều người ấy đã làm cho mình.
vi.B: Khi nàng về đến nhà mẹ chồng, Na-ô-mi hỏi: "Sao rồi con gái của mẹ?" Ru-tơ kể cho bà mọi điều người ấy đã làm cho mình.
vi.R: Khi Ru-tơ về nhà, mẹ chồng hỏi: "Con gái của mẹ, mọi việc thế nào rồi?" Ru-tơ kể cho bà mọi điều Bô-ô đã làm cho mình.

ko.L: 룻이 시어머니에게 가자, 시어머니가 말했다. "내 딸아, 너는 누구냐?" 룻은 그 사람이 자기에게 한 일을 다 시어머니에게 말했다.
ko.B: 룻이 시어머니에게 돌아오자, 나오미가 물었다. "내 딸아, 어떻게 되었느냐?" 룻은 그 사람이 자기에게 해 준 일을 모두 이야기했다.
ko.R: 룻이 집에 돌아오자, 시어머니가 물었다. "내 딸아, 일이 어떻게 되었느냐?" 룻은 보아스가 자기에게 해 준 일을 모두 말했다.

pt.L: E ela veio até a sua sogra, e ela disse: "Quem é você, minha filha?" E ela lhe contou tudo o que o homem tinha feito por ela.
pt.B: Quando ela chegou à casa da sogra, Noemi perguntou: "Como ficaram as coisas para você, minha filha?" Então Rute lhe contou tudo o que o homem tinha feito por ela.
pt.R: Quando Rute chegou em casa, a sogra lhe perguntou: "Minha filha, como estão as coisas para você agora?" Então Rute contou a ela tudo o que Boaz tinha feito por ela.

decisions.choice: who are you: how do you stand now?
alternatives: are you my daughter? (Naomi did not recognize her in the half-dark)
decisions.reason: Naomi is not asking Ruth's name. The question asks about her state: what has she become this night? Is she to be a bride? The same words are Boaz's question in the dark (verse 9), where he asks who she is.

decisions.choice: Naomi; Ruth; Boaz
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers, since both women are "she"; Readable also names "the man".

source.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר שֵׁשׁ־הַשְּׂעֹרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה נָ֣תַן לִ֑י כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י אַל־תָּב֥וֹאִי רֵיקָ֖ם אֶל־חֲמוֹתֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, these six [of] barley he gave to me, for he said to me, do not go empty to your mother-in-law.

en.L: And she said, "These six [measures of] barley he gave to me, for he said to me, 'Do not go empty to your mother-in-law.'"
en.B: She said, "He gave me these six measures of barley. 'Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed,' he told me."
en.R: Ruth said, "He gave me these six measures of barley. He told me, 'Do not go home to your mother-in-law with nothing.'"

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Vipimo hivi sita vya shayiri amenipa, kwa maana aliniambia, 'Usiende mtupu kwa mama mkwe wako.'"
sw.B: Akasema, "Amenipa vipimo hivi sita vya shayiri. Aliniambia, 'Usirudi kwa mama mkwe wako mikono mitupu.'"
sw.R: Ruthu alisema, "Amenipa vipimo hivi sita vya shayiri. Aliniambia, 'Usirudi nyumbani kwa mama mkwe wako bila kitu.'"

es.L: Y dijo: «Estas seis [medidas de] cebada me dio, porque me dijo: “No vayas vacía a tu suegra”».
es.B: Le dijo: «Me dio estas seis medidas de cebada. Me dijo: “No vuelvas a tu suegra con las manos vacías”».
es.R: Rut le dijo: «Me dio estas seis medidas de cebada. Me dijo: “No vuelvas a casa de tu suegra sin nada”».

fr.L: Et elle dit : « Ces six [mesures d’] orge, il me les a données, car il m’a dit : “Ne va pas les mains vides vers ta belle-mère.” »
fr.B: Elle dit : « Il m’a donné ces six mesures d’orge. Il m’a dit : “Ne retourne pas les mains vides chez ta belle-mère.” »
fr.R: Ruth a dit : « Il m’a donné ces six mesures d’orge. Il m’a dit : “Ne rentre pas chez ta belle-mère sans rien.” »

vi.L: Nàng nói: "Sáu [đấu] lúa mạch này ông ấy cho con, vì ông ấy nói với con: 'Đừng về tay không với mẹ chồng con.'"
vi.B: Nàng nói: "Ông ấy cho con sáu đấu lúa mạch này. Ông ấy bảo con: 'Đừng về với mẹ chồng con tay không.'"
vi.R: Ru-tơ nói: "Ông ấy cho con sáu đấu lúa mạch này. Ông ấy bảo con: 'Đừng về nhà với mẹ chồng mà không có gì.'"

ko.L: 룻이 말했다. "그분이 이 보리 여섯 [번 되어 준 것을] 저에게 주시며, '빈손으로 시어머니에게 가지 마라' 하고 말씀하셨어요."
ko.B: 룻이 말했다. "그분이 저에게 이 보리를 여섯 번 되어 주셨어요. '시어머니에게 빈손으로 돌아가지 마라' 하고 말씀하셨어요."
ko.R: 룻이 말했다. "그분이 이 보리를 여섯 번 되어 주셨어요. 그리고 '시어머니에게 빈손으로 가지 마라' 하고 말씀하셨어요."

pt.L: E ela disse: "Estas seis [medidas] de cevada ele me deu, pois ele me disse: 'Não vá vazia para a sua sogra.'"
pt.B: Ela disse: "Ele me deu estas seis medidas de cevada. 'Não volte de mãos vazias para a sua sogra', ele me disse."
pt.R: Rute disse: "Ele me deu estas seis medidas de cevada. Ele me disse: 'Não volte para a sua sogra sem nada.'"

decisions.choice: empty: the word of Naomi's grief
decisions.reason: Naomi had said, "I went away full, and the LORD has brought me back empty" (1:21). The gift, and Boaz's words about it, tell her that her emptiness is beginning to be filled. Only Ruth's report gives these words of Boaz.

decisions.choice: to me: read in the margin (qere) though not written
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the words "to me" are not written in the text but are read; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: empty-handed / with nothing
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "empty-handed" and "with nothing", which is what "empty" means here. Literal keeps "empty", so the echo of 1:21 can be seen.

decisions.choice: "tay không" for "empty"
decisions.reason: The same word Naomi used of herself in 1:21 ("tay không", "tay trắng"), so that the echo the meaning decision points out can be heard.

decisions.choice: vazia (L); de mãos vazias (B); sem nada (R)
decisions.reason: Each level takes up its own wording of Naomi's complaint in 1:21, "vazia" at Literal and Balanced and "sem nada" at Readable, so the echo of m1 can be heard at every level; Balanced says "de mãos vazias", the Portuguese idiom, which keeps the word.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ שְׁבִ֣י בִתִּ֔י עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּֽדְעִ֔ין אֵ֖יךְ יִפֹּ֣ל דָּבָ֑ר כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשְׁקֹט֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ כִּֽי־אִם־כִּלָּ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, sit, my daughter, until you know how will fall [the] matter, for will not rest the man unless he has finished the matter today.

en.L: And she said, "Sit [still], my daughter, until you know how the matter will fall, for the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today."
en.B: Naomi said, "Stay here quietly, my daughter, until you know how things fall out. The man will not rest until he has brought the matter to an end today."
en.R: Naomi said, "Be patient, my daughter, and see how it all ends. Boaz will not take any rest today until he has dealt with this."

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Kaa [kimya], binti yangu, mpaka ujue jinsi jambo hili litakavyoangukia, kwa maana mtu huyo hatatulia asipolimaliza jambo hili leo."
sw.B: Naomi alisema, "Kaa hapa kwa utulivu, binti yangu, mpaka ujue mambo yatakavyokwenda. Mtu huyo hatapumzika mpaka amelimaliza jambo hili leo."
sw.R: Naomi alisema, "Vumilia, binti yangu, uone jinsi yote yatakavyoishia. Boazi hatapumzika leo mpaka amelishughulikia jambo hili."

es.L: Y ella dijo: «Siéntate, hija mía, hasta que sepas cómo cae el asunto, porque el hombre no descansará hasta que haya terminado el asunto hoy».
es.B: Noemí le dijo: «Quédate tranquila, hija mía, hasta que sepas cómo se resuelve esto. Ese hombre no descansará hasta dejar hoy mismo arreglado el asunto».
es.R: Noemí le dijo: «Ten paciencia, hija mía, y espera a ver cómo termina todo. Booz no va a descansar hoy hasta que haya arreglado esto».

fr.L: Et elle dit : « Reste assise, ma fille, jusqu’à ce que tu saches comment l’affaire tombera, car l’homme ne se reposera pas qu’il n’ait achevé l’affaire aujourd’hui. »
fr.B: Noémi dit : « Reste tranquille, ma fille, jusqu’à ce que tu saches comment les choses vont tourner. Cet homme ne se reposera pas avant d’avoir réglé l’affaire aujourd’hui même. »
fr.R: Noémi a dit : « Sois patiente, ma fille, et attends de voir comment tout cela va finir. Booz ne va pas se reposer aujourd’hui avant d’avoir réglé cette affaire. »

vi.L: Bà nói: "Con gái của mẹ, hãy ngồi [yên] cho đến khi con biết việc sẽ ra sao, vì người ấy sẽ không nghỉ ngơi cho đến khi giải quyết xong việc này hôm nay."
vi.B: Na-ô-mi nói: "Con gái của mẹ, hãy ở yên đây cho đến khi con biết việc sẽ ra sao. Người ấy sẽ không nghỉ cho đến khi giải quyết xong việc này ngay hôm nay."
vi.R: Na-ô-mi nói: "Con gái của mẹ, hãy kiên nhẫn chờ xem mọi việc sẽ kết thúc thế nào. Hôm nay Bô-ô sẽ không nghỉ ngơi cho đến khi lo xong việc này."

ko.L: 나오미가 말했다. "내 딸아, 일이 어떻게 되는지 알 때까지 [가만히] 앉아 있어라. 그 사람은 오늘 이 일을 끝내지 않고는 쉬지 않을 것이다."
ko.B: 나오미가 말했다. "내 딸아, 일이 어떻게 될지 알게 될 때까지 조용히 기다려라. 그 사람은 오늘 이 일을 마무리 짓기 전에는 쉬지 않을 것이다."
ko.R: 나오미가 말했다. "내 딸아, 참고 기다려 보아라. 일이 어떻게 끝나는지 보자. 보아스는 오늘 이 일을 다 처리하기 전에는 쉬지 않을 것이다."

pt.L: E ela disse: "Fique sentada, minha filha, até você saber como cairá a questão, pois o homem não descansará sem ter acabado a questão hoje."
pt.B: Noemi disse: "Fique aqui tranquila, minha filha, até saber como as coisas vão terminar. Esse homem não vai sossegar enquanto não resolver o assunto hoje mesmo."
pt.R: Noemi disse: "Tenha paciência, minha filha, e espere para ver como tudo vai terminar. Boaz não vai descansar hoje enquanto não resolver isso."

decisions.choice: sit; how the matter will fall: wait and see how it turns out
decisions.reason: "Sit" means stay quietly and wait. "How a matter falls" means how it turns out. Ruth has done her part; the rest is in Boaz's hands.

decisions.choice: he will not rest unless he has finished it today
decisions.reason: Naomi is sure Boaz will act at once. The next chapter bears her out: he goes straight to the town gate (4:1).

decisions.choice: Stay here quietly / Be patient; fall out / ends
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "sit" and "fall" mean (decision m1); Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.
